newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-Tyson defeat improves Tua's chances - Barry.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Tyson defeat improves Tua's chances - Barry.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Nov 11 - Evander Holyfield's stunning upset of World Boxing Association champion Mike Tyson has improved New Zealander David Tua's chances of a shot at a world heavyweight crown, Tua's manager Kevin Barry, said on Monday.
Barry told NZPA the opportunity might come as soon as the next 12 to 18 months.
He said Tyson's defeat in Las Vegas yesterday meant controversial promoter Don King had lost his grip on the heavyweight division.
Instead, control had switched to the Lou Duva camp, whose company, Main Events, handles Holyfield, IBF world champion Michael Moorer, leading WBC contender Lennox Lewis, as well as Tua.
"It's absolutely great news for David Tua," Barry said.
"With the strength that Main Events now has in being in control of the division, it's going to make things so much easier for David to get a chance to fight for the title."
Tua, who is 25-0 with 21 knockouts since turning professional, will have his next bout against Nigerian David Izonritei in Connecticut next month.
Izonritei was the last man to beat the Aucklander, outpointing him in their semifinal at the 1992 Barcelona Games before going on to take silver against Cuban star Felix Savon.
"It's not a huge fight, because Tua is heavily favoured to win with the improvement he has made in the last four years," Barry said.
"Then he is going to have a fight here in New Zealand in February."
After that, Tua's opposition will go up a level.
"He is now the No 8 ranked by the WBC, and we will step David up after that to fight a fighter ranked higher than him," Barry said.
"If he comes through that, there is every chance within 12 to 18 months he will get a shot at the heavyweight championship of the world."
Tua, similar in build to Tyson, was called in to spar with Holyfield, who said after reclaiming the title: "My sparring partner was whupping me up.
"It was disconcerting to know you're supposed to fight Mike Tyson and you can't go but two or three rounds sparring."
Barry hadn't yet heard the comments himself, but he wasn't surprised.
"In one of the sparring sessions David had, it was supposed to be four rounds," he said.
"But it was stopped after three rounds because David was repeatedly hitting him."
